\section{\texttt{benchmarking}}
\label{module:feedback_intelligence_agent.benchmarking}\index{Modules!benchmarking}

Latency and throughput benchmarks for the RAG pipeline.
\apifield{Source}\texttt{src/\allowbreak{}feedback\_\allowbreak{}intelligence\_\allowbreak{}agent/\allowbreak{}benchmarking.\allowbreak{}py}, 286 lines
\apifield{Imports}\texttt{agent}, \texttt{chunking}, \texttt{config}, \texttt{embeddings}, \texttt{evaluation}, \texttt{factory}, \texttt{ingestion}, \texttt{vector\_\allowbreak{}store}
\apifield{Classes}\cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.benchmarking.PhaseStats}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.benchmarking.BenchmarkReport}
\apifield{Functions}\cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.benchmarking.percentile}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.benchmarking.summarize}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.benchmarking.run_benchmark}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.benchmarking.report_to_markdown}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.benchmarking.write_benchmark_outputs}
\apifield{Constants}\texttt{RESULTS\_\allowbreak{}JSON\_\allowbreak{}FILENAME}, \texttt{RESULTS\_\allowbreak{}MARKDOWN\_\allowbreak{}FILENAME}, \texttt{PHASE\_\allowbreak{}INDEXING}, \texttt{PHASE\_\allowbreak{}EMBEDDING}, \texttt{PHASE\_\allowbreak{}RETRIEVAL}, \texttt{PHASE\_\allowbreak{}AGENT\_\allowbreak{}RESPONSE}
\apifield{Details}This module times the four phases that dominate end-to-end cost in a retrieval system and reports robust summary statistics per phase:

- \texttt{indexing}: load the CSV, chunk it, embed every chunk, and build the in-memory vector store (one timed unit per repetition). - \texttt{embedding}: embed the benchmark queries with the hashing embedding model. - \texttt{retrieval}: run every query through the retriever and collect the top-k chunks. - \texttt{agent\_\allowbreak{}response}: run every query through the full agent (retrieval plus answer generation with the deterministic local provider).

Each phase is run \texttt{warmup} times to prime caches and then \texttt{repetitions} times for measurement. Durations come from \texttt{time.\allowbreak{}perf\_\allowbreak{}counter}, so they are wall-clock times and inherently non-deterministic. Only the *structure* of the report is deterministic; never snapshot the timing values.

The summary statistics (mean, median, p95, min, max) are exposed as pure functions so they can be unit-tested without timing anything. Results serialise to both JSON and a small Markdown table via \texttt{write\_\allowbreak{}benchmark\_\allowbreak{}outputs}.

\section{\texttt{experiments}}
\label{module:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments}\index{Modules!experiments}

Repeatable experiment runner for comparing RAG configurations.
\apifield{Source}\texttt{src/\allowbreak{}feedback\_\allowbreak{}intelligence\_\allowbreak{}agent/\allowbreak{}experiments.\allowbreak{}py}, 346 lines
\apifield{Imports}\texttt{agent}, \texttt{chunking}, \texttt{config}, \texttt{embeddings}, \texttt{evaluation}, \texttt{factory}, \texttt{ingestion}, \texttt{vector\_\allowbreak{}store}
\apifield{Classes}\cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.ExperimentConfig}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.QueryResult}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.AggregateMetrics}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.ExperimentResult}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.RunMetadata}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.ExperimentTrackingError}
\apifield{Functions}\cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.run_experiment}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.collect_run_metadata}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.write_experiment_outputs}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.experiments.track_experiment_run}
\apifield{Constants}\texttt{RESULTS\_\allowbreak{}FILENAME}, \texttt{METRICS\_\allowbreak{}FILENAME}, \texttt{METADATA\_\allowbreak{}FILENAME}, \texttt{TrackingProvider}
\apifield{Details}An experiment is described by a YAML file (parsed into a typed \texttt{ExperimentConfig}), executed fully locally against a feedback CSV and a JSONL query set, and persisted as three JSON artifacts:

- \texttt{results.\allowbreak{}json}: configuration plus per-query answers and metrics. - \texttt{metrics.\allowbreak{}json}: aggregate retrieval and answer-quality metrics. - \texttt{run\_\allowbreak{}metadata.\allowbreak{}json}: timestamp, git commit, Python and package versions.

With the deterministic local LLM provider, \texttt{results.\allowbreak{}json} and \texttt{metrics.\allowbreak{}json} are bit-for-bit reproducible; everything environment-specific lives in \texttt{run\_\allowbreak{}metadata.\allowbreak{}json}. This makes experiment outputs directly comparable across configurations and usable as CI regression baselines.

\section{\texttt{guardrails}}
\label{module:feedback_intelligence_agent.guardrails}\index{Modules!guardrails}

Deterministic safety guardrails for the feedback intelligence agent.
\apifield{Source}\texttt{src/\allowbreak{}feedback\_\allowbreak{}intelligence\_\allowbreak{}agent/\allowbreak{}guardrails.\allowbreak{}py}, 220 lines
\apifield{Classes}\cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.guardrails.GuardrailDecision}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.guardrails.GuardrailRule}
\apifield{Functions}\cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.guardrails.check_input}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.guardrails.is_suspicious_context}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.guardrails.check_context}
\apifield{Constants}\texttt{Severity}, \texttt{SAFE\_\allowbreak{}REFUSAL}, \texttt{INPUT\_\allowbreak{}RULES}
\apifield{Details}The module implements two transparent, regex/keyword-based gates:

1. \texttt{check\_\allowbreak{}input} runs **before retrieval** and blocks empty queries, prompt-injection attempts, requests for hidden system instructions, requests to ignore the retrieved context, and unsupported data access requests (other customers' PII, raw database access). 2. \texttt{check\_\allowbreak{}context} runs **before answer generation** and flags retrieved chunks that contain instruction-override content (indirect prompt injection planted in feedback text).

Every rule is a documented regular expression, so decisions are fully deterministic, reproducible in CI, and easy to audit. No model call is involved in any guardrail decision.

\apibreak
\section{\texttt{jobs}}
\label{module:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs}\index{Modules!jobs}

Asynchronous ingestion jobs with status tracking.
\apifield{Source}\texttt{src/\allowbreak{}feedback\_\allowbreak{}intelligence\_\allowbreak{}agent/\allowbreak{}jobs.\allowbreak{}py}, 281 lines
\apifield{Exports}\texttt{InMemoryJobStore}, \texttt{JobNotFoundError}, \texttt{JobRequest}, \texttt{JobResult}, \texttt{JobStatus}, \texttt{JobStore}, \texttt{JsonJobStore}, \texttt{new\_\allowbreak{}job\_\allowbreak{}id}, \texttt{run\_\allowbreak{}ingestion\_\allowbreak{}job}
\apifield{Imports}\texttt{chunking}, \texttt{data\_\allowbreak{}contracts}, \texttt{embeddings}, \texttt{factory}, \texttt{ingestion}, \texttt{telemetry}, \texttt{vector\_\allowbreak{}store}
\apifield{Classes}\cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs.JobStatus}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs.JobRequest}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs.JobResult}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs.JobStore}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs.JobNotFoundError}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs.InMemoryJobStore}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs.JsonJobStore}
\apifield{Functions}\cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs.new_job_id}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.jobs.run_ingestion_job}
\apifield{Details}This module decouples ingestion from the request/response cycle. A client submits an ingestion request, receives a job identifier immediately, and polls for the terminal status (\texttt{succeeded} / \texttt{failed}) without blocking on the embedding and indexing work.

The pieces are:

1. Typed job models (\texttt{JobStatus}, \texttt{JobRequest}, \texttt{JobResult}). 2. A \texttt{JobStore} protocol with two backends: an in-memory store guarded by a lock (suitable for FastAPI \texttt{BackgroundTasks}) and a JSON-backed store that persists one file per job. 3. A single \texttt{run\_\allowbreak{}ingestion\_\allowbreak{}job} pipeline that loads + validates a CSV, chunks it, builds embeddings, persists the vector store, and records success or a clean failure message. The full exception detail is logged server-side but never surfaced to the client, so secrets, stack traces, and filesystem internals do not leak.

The pipeline is a plain function so it is directly unit-testable and is also the exact callable scheduled by the API's \texttt{BackgroundTasks}.

\section{\texttt{memory}}
\label{module:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory}\index{Modules!memory}

Conversation memory and follow-up query rewriting.
\apifield{Source}\texttt{src/\allowbreak{}feedback\_\allowbreak{}intelligence\_\allowbreak{}agent/\allowbreak{}memory.\allowbreak{}py}, 344 lines
\apifield{Imports}\texttt{llm}
\apifield{Classes}\cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.ConversationTurn}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.ConversationMemory}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.ConversationStore}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.InMemoryConversationStore}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.JsonConversationStore}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.QueryRewrite}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.QueryRewriter}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.DeterministicQueryRewriter}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.LLMQueryRewriter}
\apifield{Functions}\cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.new_conversation_id}, \cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.memory.extract_entities}
\apifield{Details}The module provides three building blocks:

1. Typed conversation state (\texttt{ConversationTurn}, \texttt{ConversationMemory}) that records what the user asked, what the agent answered, and which documents grounded the answer. 2. Pluggable persistence (\texttt{InMemoryConversationStore} for tests and \texttt{JsonConversationStore} for local JSON files under \texttt{.\allowbreak{}artifacts/\allowbreak{}}). 3. Deterministic follow-up query rewriting (\texttt{DeterministicQueryRewriter}) that converts elliptical follow-ups ("What about pricing?") and pronoun references ("Why do they complain about it?") into standalone questions using only entities from the previous turn. Only the rewritten standalone question reaches retrieval, so the index is never queried with the full conversation history. An optional \texttt{LLMQueryRewriter} can delegate rewriting to an LLM provider, but the deterministic local rewriter is the default and requires no external APIs.

Ratings are derived from the chosen sentiment so the dataset is internally consistent.

\apifield{Details}The module provides two layers:

1. Lightweight JSON logging helpers (\texttt{configure\_\allowbreak{}logging}, \texttt{log\_\allowbreak{}event}) that keep runtime logs consistent and easy to redirect to systems such as CloudWatch, Datadog, or OpenTelemetry collectors. 2. A structured telemetry pipeline (\texttt{Telemetry} plus pluggable sinks) that records spans and events with timestamps, durations, and correlation IDs. Telemetry is a no-op unless a sink is attached, so the default code path stays free of side effects.

\apibreak
\section{\texttt{tools}}
\label{module:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools}\index{Modules!tools}

Deterministic tool-use framework for the feedback intelligence agent.
\apifield{Source}\texttt{src/\allowbreak{}feedback\_\allowbreak{}intelligence\_\allowbreak{}agent/\allowbreak{}tools.\allowbreak{}py}, 565 lines
\apifield{Imports}\texttt{citations}, \texttt{schemas}
\apifield{Classes}\cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.ToolError}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.ToolOutput}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.Tool}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.SentimentSummaryInput}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.SentimentSummaryOutput}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.SentimentSummaryTool}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.IssueClusterInput}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.IssueCluster}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.IssueClusterOutput}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.IssueClusterTool}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.TicketEvidence}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.TicketDraftInput}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.TicketDraftOutput}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.TicketDraftTool}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.ToolRegistry}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.ToolSelection}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.ToolRoute}, \cref{class:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.ToolRouter}
\apifield{Functions}\cref{func:feedback_intelligence_agent.tools.build_default_tools}
\apifield{Constants}\texttt{ISSUE\_\allowbreak{}TERM\_\allowbreak{}GROUPS}, \texttt{TOOL\_\allowbreak{}ROUTES}
\apifield{Details}The module provides:

1. A typed tool interface (\texttt{Tool}) where every tool declares a name, a description, a Pydantic input schema, and a Pydantic output schema. 2. Three local tools that run fully offline: \texttt{SentimentSummaryTool}, \texttt{IssueClusterTool}, and \texttt{TicketDraftTool}. 3. A registry (\texttt{ToolRegistry}) and a deterministic keyword router (\texttt{ToolRouter}) that selects at most one tool per query.

No function-calling API is involved: routing and execution are keyword and rule based, so tool behaviour is reproducible in tests and CI. Unknown or unavailable tool requests are surfaced as a graceful refusal instead of an error, and the agent falls back to the plain RAG answer.
